language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<margin>ᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠶᠡᠷᠡᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</margin>
<margin>諸品經第十八卷上三百九十二</margin>
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠦᠵᠦᠭᠦᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠣᠷᠴᠢᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠨ ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠳᠤ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠃ ᠮᠥᠨ <unclear>ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ</unclear>
ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠰᠡᠳᠭᠢᠯ ᠦᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠪᠠ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠨ ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠭᠡᠶᠢᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ
ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡᠳ ᠂ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠭᠠᠯᠠᠪ ᠤᠳ ᠲᠤ ᠪᠣᠳᠢ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠳᠠᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ
ᠡᠭᠦᠰᠭᠡᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠴᠢᠭᠤᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰᠭᠡᠵᠦ ᠃ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠃
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠬᠢᠵᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠬᠦᠷᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ
ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠂ ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠳᠡᠬᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ
ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠲᠤᠷ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ
ᠪᠠ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠃ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤᠷᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠴᠢ ᠃ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ ᠃
ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠂ ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠃ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠃
ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ ᠃ ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠃
ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠠ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠃ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠦ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ
ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠃ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ
ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠰᠡᠳᠭᠢᠯ ᠦᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠪᠠ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠳᠠᠯ ᠢ <unclear>ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ</unclear>
ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠂ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠰᠡᠳᠭᠢᠯ ᠦᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ <unclear>ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠴᠢ</unclear> ᠪᠤᠢ ᠃
ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠦ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠰᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ <unclear>ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ</unclear>
ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠴᠢ ᠂ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠰᠡᠳᠭᠢᠯ ᠢ <unclear>ᠠᠷᠢᠯᠭᠠᠭᠴᠢ</unclear>
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠃ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ <unclear>ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ</unclear>
ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠃ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠶᠢᠷᠲᠢᠨᠴᠦ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠲᠤᠰᠠ
ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠴᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠂ ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠃
ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠡᠬᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ
ᠡᠨᠡ ᠮᠡᠲᠦ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠃ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ
ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠰᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ <unclear>ᠬᠦᠷᠳᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠡᠷᠭᠢᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ</unclear>
ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠃ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠲᠤ <unclear>ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ</unclear> ᠃
<vocab>ᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪ, 諸品經, ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ, ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ, ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ, ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ, ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ</vocab>

<margin>Miscellaneous <note>original: "Eldeb", the Miscellaneous Sutras section of the Mongolian Kanjur</note>, upper, three hundred ninety-two</margin>
<margin>Sutras of Various Sections <note>original: "Zhupin jing"</note>, Fascicle Eighteen, upper, three hundred ninety-two</margin>
abided in the ocean of <term>orčilang</term> <gloss>cyclic existence, samsara</gloss>, boundless onward and beyond. Truly <unclear>ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ</unclear>
illuminating the mental actions of all sentient beings with the light of <term>bilig</term> <gloss>transcendent wisdom, prajna</gloss>,
and having practiced the conduct of <term>bodi</term> <gloss>awakening, bodhi</gloss> throughout measureless <term>galab</term> <gloss>cosmic eons, kalpas</gloss>,
perfecting the accumulation of <term>buyan</term> <gloss>merit, punya</gloss> that was generated and cultivated. All are present.
Having proclaimed that he attained the wisdom of the <term>Burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha, the Awakened One</gloss> that has reached the further shore <note>a translation of the Sanskrit concept of paramita, perfection</note>,
having revealed that which has arisen from other times and that which has become beyond ordinary comprehension,
having thoroughly revealed the <term>nom-un činar</term> <gloss>true nature of phenomena, dharmata</gloss> of all phenomena
and having become the realm of the Buddha. Having manifested the <term>mön činar</term> <gloss>intrinsic nature, svabhava</gloss>,
he is the one who brings all <term>amitan</term> <gloss>sentient beings</gloss> to maturity. Furthermore, all <term>nom-ud</term> <gloss>phenomena or teachings, dharmas</gloss> are perceived.
Having come to be, they are truly devoid of inherent nature. Such are all phenomena.
All phenomena that have abided and come into being: they are truly perfected.
What is enacted herein, having become devoid of nature and <term>belge</term> <gloss>characteristic mark, lakshana</gloss>,
has been revealed beyond. Therefore, all phenomena
are truly the wisdom of the Buddha. Revealed through intrinsic nature,
the mental actions and conduct of all sentient beings <unclear>ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ</unclear>
having come to be, the true nature of the mind itself <unclear>ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠴᠢ</unclear> is.
Therefore, the one who equally reveals all phenomena <unclear>ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ</unclear>
the one who acts to reveal, the minds of all sentient beings <unclear>ᠠᠷᠢᠯᠭᠠᠭᠴᠢ</unclear>
has gone beyond. Through the wisdom of the <term>Tegünčilen Iregsen</term> <gloss>Thus-Gone One, Tathagata</gloss> <unclear>ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ</unclear>
having abided. To all sentient beings of the <term>yirtinčü</term> <gloss>world, loka</gloss>,
he has become a benefactor, and he has truly revealed it.
Beginning from the time it came to be, revealing the true nature of all phenomena,
thus he revealed all phenomena. Furthermore, for all
sentient beings' benefit, of the teaching <unclear>ᠬᠦᠷᠳᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠡᠷᠭᠢᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ</unclear>
having enacted. In the intrinsic nature <unclear>ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ</unclear>.

<summary>This folio recto from the Miscellaneous Sutras section of the Mongolian Kanjur expounds Mahayana Buddhist doctrine on the emptiness of phenomena and the illuminating wisdom of the Buddha. It describes how the Tathagata perfects merit across measureless eons to mature sentient beings and reveal the true nature of reality.</summary>
<keywords>Mongolian Kanjur, Mahayana Buddhism, transcendent wisdom, true nature of phenomena, emptiness, Tathagata, accumulation of merit, cyclic existence, sentient beings</keywords>
